children.translated_text: Just as food or a substance passes into the bodily constituents by means of a suitable vehicle,
so, through the krāmaṇa operation, the king of rasas enters metals.
With magnetite, poison, rasaka, realgar, red oil, indragopikā insects, and the like,
this excellent krāmaṇa should always be applied in smearing and in casting.
Kunaṭī, pyrites, poison, human blood, and crow droppings,
and the ear-wax of buffalo cows and woman's milk are strength-giving in krāmaṇa.
Great blood joined with borax, kunaṭī, rāmaṭha, and bhūmilatā
is declared to be this krāmaṇa, always to be applied in smearing and in casting.

children.text: śilayā nihato nāgo vaṅgaṃ vā tālakena śuddhena
children.translated_text: Lead struck down with realgar, or tin with purified orpiment,
respectively for yellow and white metal, is designated as this krāmaṇa.

children.text: tīkṣṇaṃ daradena hataṃ śulbaṃ vā tāpyamāritaṃ vidhinā
children.translated_text: Iron killed with realgar, or copper killed according to rule with tāpya,
is declared to be this krāmaṇa, with magnetite as its chief ingredient, or else with pyrites.

children.text: mākṣikasattvaṃ nāgaṃ vihāya na krāmaṇaṃ kimapyasti
children.translated_text: Apart from pyrite-sattva and lead, there is no krāmaṇa at all.

children.text: dalasiddhe rasasiddhe vidhāvasau bhavati khalu saphalaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When the leaf is perfected and the rasa is perfected, that procedure truly becomes fruitful.

children.text: anayā khalu sāraṇayā krāmaṇena ca viśati yojito vidhivat
children.translated_text: By this sāraṇa and by krāmaṇa, when applied according to rule, it enters indeed;
without the procedure of vedha, mercury does not manifest its own qualities.
Rasa, realgar, tāpya, sulfur, orpiment, lapis lazuli, and stainless material,
with copper killed by puṭa and expelled in silver: this is the drawing-out of gold.
There should be ninety-eight parts of silver, but one part of gold,
and one part of mercury; this is known as the hundredth-part procedure.
Here likewise there are forty-nine parts of silver and of copper,
one part of gold, and the vedha is done with one part of mercury.
Thus the thousandfold piercer and the crorefold piercer are employed,
after knowing the strength and weakness of the mercury according to the digestion-seed.
Having first added a counter-casting, by treatment with lac, fish bile, and the like,

children.text: tāre vā śulbe vā tārāriṣṭe tathā kṛṣṭau ||
children.translated_text: whether in silver, in copper, in alloyed silver, or likewise in drawn-out gold,
then, when it has been rubbed with krāmaṇa, with that paste and also with mercury made into a lump,
and when it is very much melted, that vedha is performed by kuntavedha.
One should cover it with cloth moistened with that oil, or with flesh, or with ash,
for the sake of the krāmaṇa of the king mercury into the substance to be pierced according to rule.

children.text: iti sāritasya kathitaṃ rasasya vedhādi krāmaṇaṃ karma
children.translated_text: Thus the krāmaṇa operation beginning with vedha has been taught for mercury that has been made sārita.
When the seed has been digested from a quarter and so on, it is applied by smearing on sheets.
A very pure sheet of alloyed silver and the like, rubbed with sour substances and so forth,

children.text: ālipya rasena tataḥ krāmaṇalipte puṭeṣu viśrāntam ||
children.translated_text: is then smeared with mercury and left to rest in puṭas coated with krāmaṇa.

children.text: ardhena miśrayitvā hemnā jyeṣṭhena taddalaṃ puṭitam
children.translated_text: After mixing that sheet with half as much excellent gold, it is heated by puṭa;
then this color-puṭa should be given with earth, khaga, salt, blood, and clay.
Powder of bhūpativartaka, repeatedly treated with the juice of śirīṣa flowers,
immediately makes white gold red with an eightieth part.
Rasa, realgar, stainless material, tāpya, salt, realgar, pyrites, and nṛpa,
together with coral, kaṅkuṣṭha, borax, and ochre as counter-castings, make white gold.
Moistened with the juice of tāpībhava, nṛpāvarta, bīja, and pūra,
by puṭa-cooking it makes gold resemble vermilion.
One should carry tin-mica, white pyrites, or śaila into white metal;

children.text: tattāraṃ ca daśāṃśena tārotkarṣaṃ karoti hi ||
children.translated_text: and that silver, with a tenth part, indeed produces the improvement of silver.

children.text: nāgaḥ karoti mṛdutāṃ nirvyūḍhastāṃ ca raktatāṃ ca raviḥ
children.translated_text: Lead brings about softness, and, when carried through, it brings that redness; the sun-metal does so too.

children.text: tāṃ pītatāṃ ca tīkṣṇaṃ kācastatkālikavināśaṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: It also brings that yellowness, sharpness, and the immediate destruction of the glassy impurity.
If it is moistened with karañja oil together with gold-red mākṣika and then blown in the fire,

children.text: pāte pāte daśa daśa vindati yāvaddhi koṭimapi ||
children.translated_text: at each casting, ten by ten, it attains even up to a crore-fold power.
And this, when very thoroughly melted and repeatedly sprinkled with kaṃguṇī oil,
pierces gold with a hundredth part by means of a casting of mākṣika and sun-metal.
Copper struck down, and khaga that has been struck by mercury and sulfur and made yellow, with a tenth part,

children.text: vidhyati kanakaṃ kurute tannirvyūḍhaṃ marditaṃ sudṛḍham ||
children.translated_text: pierces gold; when strongly rubbed, it makes that carried-through gold firm.
Mercury, after consuming well-blown gold equal to rasaka and then with a coating of arka and moon-metal,

children.text: mākṣikasattvaṃ hemnā karoti jīrṇo rasaḥ śatāṃśena ||
children.translated_text: being digested, makes mākṣika-sattva into gold with a hundredth part.
Dead copper, eight times as much, smeared on purified silver with a closed crucible,
when digested with a sixteenth part of that, pierces silver with half a hundredth part.

children.text: āvṛtya kanakakariṇau śilayā prativāpitau tato bhuktvā
children.translated_text: After covering the gold and the elephant-metal with stone and giving counter-castings, and then after consuming them,
mercury digested with sulfur in a dolā-yantra becomes a ten-percent piercer in silver.
Mercury that has digested the six metals killed by the enemy and has remained in grain for four months,
together with copper and surā, pierces bell-metal with a hundredth part.

children.text: vakṣye samprati samyagyad bījaṃ samarase jīrṇam
children.translated_text: Now I shall properly explain the bīja that is digested in equal mercury,
and the procedure of piṣṭi, stambha, and so on, as it is being revealed; listen, wise ones.
With lapis lazuli, vimala, yellow mica, sulfur, tāpya, and rasaka,
and furnished with kāṅkṣī, kāsīsa, orpiment, and realgar, lead is to be combined.

children.text: ahimārarasaiḥ puṭitaṃ māraya nāgaṃ nirutthakaṃ yāvat
children.translated_text: Puṭa-cooked with the juices of ahimāra, kill the lead until it becomes unable to rise again.

children.text: tadanu ca tasya hi madhye śulbaṃ gandhaṃ ca lavaṇakaṃkuṣṭham ||
children.translated_text: After that, in the middle of it place copper, sulfur, salt, and kaṅkuṣṭha.
Treat all that a hundred times with the juices of ripe arka leaves,
and in copper drawn out from bell-metal one should expel the powder hundreds of times.

children.text: śulbena tena hi samaṃ rasakapītābhrasatvavimalaṃ ca
children.translated_text: Equal to that copper are rasaka, yellow mica-sattva, and vimala,
ochre, mākṣika-sattva, borax, and lead, joined with sharp iron.
Having made dvandva compounds with these, one should color the copper by a casting of mākṣika.
Even twenty times, when it is melted, one should then sprinkle it.
After making a mixture of the juices of nirguṇḍī, kākamācī, and kanyā,

children.text: vārān sapta ca vidhinā tadapi ca nirvāpayeddhemni ||
children.translated_text: seven times according to rule, one should also quench that in gold.
Until it colors the excellent bīja twenty-four-fold,

children.text: pakvaṃ mākṣikameva hi tena ca vidhinā tadapi caturviṃśatiguṇam ||
children.translated_text: it is indeed cooked mākṣika; and by that same procedure that too becomes twenty-four-fold.
A small measure of that bīja should first be put into the prepared king of rasas,

children.text: mūṣāyāṃ khalu dattvā daśaguṇaṃ ca gandhakaṃ dāhyam ||
children.translated_text: and in a crucible ten times as much sulfur is to be placed and burned.
Or else, in a firm sand-apparatus, in a crucible fourteen fingers high,
having placed the mercury in the middle, it is sealed with the application of a lighter puṭa.

children.text: tena samaṃ bījavare piṣṭiḥ pādāṃśataḥ kāryā
children.translated_text: With that excellent bīja, a piṣṭi should be made in the proportion of one quarter.
After placing the piṣṭikā inside a crucible measuring nine fingers,
it is to be covered all around with lumps made of nirguṇḍī, kākamācī, gojihvā, dugdhikā, raktā,
gṛhakanyā, honey, and rock salt.
The puṭa application should be made until it attains firmness.
Sulfur, orpiment, kāṅkṣī, kāsīsa, salt, and alkali, six times as much,
and tāpya equal to all that, are to be placed outside as the medicinal lump.
Then, after putting the piṣṭi in the kacchapa apparatus with sixfold and again sixfold additions,

children.text: svedyaṃ puṭayogena tu tridinaṃ ghaṭikātrayaṃ yāvat
children.translated_text: it should be steamed by the puṭa application for three days, for three ghaṭikās at a time.

children.text: uddhṛtya tato yatnāt piṣṭvā sucūrṇitāṃ kṛtvā ||
children.translated_text: Then, carefully taking it out, one should grind it and make it into a fine powder.

children.text: samabījena tu sāryo nāgaṃ triguṇaṃ tataḥ samuttārya
children.translated_text: It is to be caused to flow with an equal bīja; then one should bring out lead three times as much.
Pratisāraṇā is then to be performed with digested mercury joined with bīja.
Anusāraṇā follows afterward, where the bīja becomes threefold.
Over that previously described substance, dead lead a hundred times as much is to be carried.

children.text: tena ca ghoṣākṛṣṭe śulbe vedho'tha saptaśataiḥ ||
children.translated_text: By that, in copper drawn out from bell-metal, the vedha is then seven-hundredfold.
This krāmaṇa is also prepared first with mākṣika, realgar, sulfur, and orpiment,
with lapis lazuli, vimala, coral, kaṅkuṣṭha, tuttha, and poisons,
with magnetite, ochre, borax, bhūmilatā, blood, and the juices of indragopa insects,

children.text: mahiṣīṇāṃ karṇamalair mṛtalohaṃ vāyasasya viṣṭhā ca ||
children.translated_text: with the ear-wax of buffalo cows, dead metal, and crow droppings,

children.text: pārāvatasya viṣṭhā strīpayaḥ sarvam ekataḥ kṛtvā
children.translated_text: with pigeon droppings and woman's milk, all made into one mixture.
This krāmaṇa paste should be treated a hundred times with the red and yellow groups,
in kaṃguṇī oil, and with seven treatments of krauñcī bile.

children.text: kalkenānena pacet sāritapiṣṭiṃ ca haṇḍikāyāṃ hi ||
children.translated_text: With this paste one should cook the sārita piṣṭi in a small pot,

children.text: yāvadraktā bhavati hi gacchati nāgaṃ samuttārya
children.translated_text: until it becomes red and, when brought out, goes into lead.
To that extent one should add an addition in all the sāraṇa and related operations.

children.text: evaṃ hi koṭivedhī rasarājaḥ krāmito bhūtvā
children.translated_text: Thus the king of rasas, having been made to undergo krāmaṇa, becomes a crore-fold piercer.
Having become a giver of increase in virility and the like, it bestows enjoyments.
Mica, mākṣika, and gold, mixed with lead according to rule,
are to be made into a piṣṭi in mercury and puṭa-cooked with a preparation of divine herbs.
There is a burning with sixfold sulfur; after bringing out the lead with orpiment,
in silver the drawing-out of gold, when combined, occurs with a sixteenth part.

children.text: mākṣikanihataṃ śulbaṃ śilayā nihataṃ ca nāgatulyāṃśam
children.translated_text: Copper killed with mākṣika, and also lead in an equal part killed with orpiment,
puṭa-cooked with citron juices and together with rock salt, should be cooked in an earthen pot.
That powder, together with ghee, honey, and borax, is placed in a sealed crucible.
When carried threefold into silver, there arises a marvelous drawing-out of gold.

children.text: śulbaṃ balinā nihataṃ tīkṣṇaṃ daradena nihatasamabhāgam
children.translated_text: Copper, killed with balin and sharp material killed with realgar in an equal part,
should be made into one and cooked by puṭa-heating, with only the mother-rasa.
When drawn out in silver at three times the amount, it becomes like a cat's eye in appearance;

children.text: liptaṃ rasena puṭitaṃ hemārdhena mātrayā tulyam ||
children.translated_text: smeared with mercury and heated by puṭa, it is equal in measure to half as much gold.

children.text: liptaṃ tadanu puṭitaṃ nāgaṃ hi rasena pādayuktena
children.translated_text: After that, lead smeared and heated by puṭa with mercury, with a quarter part added,

children.text: kharparakasthaṃ kṛtvā kāryaṃ vidhinā dṛḍhaṃ tāpyam ||
children.translated_text: should be placed in a crucible of kharparaka and heated strongly according to rule.
Treated with the juice of nirguṇḍī, heated by puṭa, rolled smooth with stone,
it should be rubbed and heated by puṭa until it reaches the state of non-rising.
When that, drawn out in silver, has become beautifully yellow,
and is mixed with an equal amount of gold, it becomes gold equal in measure.

children.text: tāpyaṃ cāṃgulisaṃjñaṃ cūrṇaṃ kṛtvā tadantare dattvā
children.translated_text: Tāpya, called aṅguli, should be made into powder and placed inside it;

children.text: śulbasya guptamūṣā kāryā puṭitāpyatha ca dhmātā ||
children.translated_text: a sealed crucible for copper should be prepared, heated by puṭa, and then blown.
Mixed with gold according to rule, it certainly becomes equal in measure.
With mercury digested from a quarter and so on, one should smear the sheets of gold-drawn metal.

children.text: krāmaṇayogena tato vilipya vidhinā nidhāya tulyādhaḥ
children.translated_text: Then, by the krāmaṇa procedure, having smeared it according to rule and placed it with an equal amount underneath,
afterwards, joined with gold, it is blown and melted together inside the crucible.
The apparatus cooked in a pot, placed in fivefold clay, is cooked by puṭa.

children.text: vakṣyāmi cālepavidhiṃ kramati ca sūto yathā hi patreṣu
children.translated_text: Now I shall explain the method of coating, by which mercury indeed passes into the sheets,
and, in brief, the procedure by which the king mercury colors them.
Having made lac-dyed cloth, smeared above with oil and then with powder,
one should make it sprinkled over with sulfur and realgar according to rule.

children.text: tadupari śṛtaṃ ca dattvā gandhakaśilācūrṇaṃ ca sūtavare
children.translated_text: Upon that, having placed what has been cooked and also sulfur-realgar powder on the excellent mercury,

children.text: paścādvartiḥ kāryā pātre dhṛtvāyase ca same ||
children.translated_text: afterwards a wick should be made and placed in an iron vessel of the same size.

children.text: dīpaṃ pratibodhya tatastailaṃ dattvā tataḥ stokam
children.translated_text: Then, having kindled the lamp and added a little oil,

children.text: pākaṃ yāmasyārdhaṃ svāṅge śītaṃ tataḥ kāryam ||
children.translated_text: it should be cooked for half a yāma; then it should be allowed to cool in its own vessel.
Then one should take the mercury-drawn metal, which is smeared with that;
having smeared it with krāmaṇa preparations and heated it by puṭa, it is blown in gold.
Or else, with realgar and orpiment, sulfur, pyrites, cooked dead lead,
together with kaṅkuṣṭha and coral, all ground in kaṅguṇī oil,

children.text: madhye sūto yukto mṛditaḥ khalve tathāyase vidhinā
children.translated_text: mercury placed in the middle is rubbed in an iron mortar according to rule;
having steamed it and placed it in a bamboo tube, it is steamed in a dolā apparatus for three days.
Having smeared the sheet with these black substances according to the previously stated procedure,

children.text: nāgaṃ dattvā prakaṭaṃ stokaṃ stokaṃ krameṇaiva ||
children.translated_text: one should add exposed lead little by little, exactly in sequence.

children.text: bhavati hi kanakaṃ divyamakṣīṇaṃ devayogyaṃ ca
children.translated_text: Then there is divine gold, imperishable and fit for the gods.

children.text: evaṃ jāritasūte sakalāḥ khalu haṇḍikāḥ sarvāḥ ||
children.translated_text: When mercury has thus been made jārita, all the small pots, indeed every one,
without seed, when it is equally digested, with only one quarter and with one sixteenth,
with half, the quarter-operation, and with one quarter, produce gold equal in amount.
I shall explain the drawing-out of silver: dead tin with an equal part of orpiment,
suspended and then blown, causes copper to bear the luster of silver.
Afterwards lead should be added in open crucibles until it is pure;

children.text: tāvad dhmātaṃ vidhinā sunirmalaṃ nistaraṅgaṃ tu ||
children.translated_text: it should be blown according to rule until it is very pure and entirely free from waves.
With orpiment, realgar, and sarjikā, with rock salt, and with nayanahita,

children.text: ekaikaṃ sahitaṃ vā vedhaṃ dattvā punaḥ śulbe ||
children.translated_text: either each one separately or combined, having given a piercing again in copper,
with goat dung, buffalo buttermilk, snuhī milk, and ghee successively,
and with mixtures of jaggery, milk, and honey, there is sprinkling successively at the piercing.

children.text: kāñcī brāhmī kuṭilaṃ tālakaṃ samabhāgayojitaṃ dhmātam
children.translated_text: Kāñcī, brāhmī, kuṭila, and orpiment, joined in equal parts and blown,
pierce copper; by this there is a divine drawing-out of silver.
Thus this silver-drawing, smeared and pierced with mercury that has been made sārita,

children.text: tāraṃ karoti vimalaṃ lepaṃ vā pādajīrṇādi ||
children.translated_text: makes stainless silver, or a coating when mercury has digested a quarter and so on.
Thus, mixed, pierced, and made to pass in, then equal to the mother-substance,
the silver leaf becomes faultless by cutting, hammering, and touchstone-testing.
Thus the method of piercing, after it has been understood by one who knows the rules of the śāstra and is skilled in work,
should be performed by one expert in operations, after learning the instruction of the guru.

children.text: iti rasarājasya vidhau vedhavidhānaṃ prasaṃgataḥ proktam
children.translated_text: Thus, in connection with the procedure of the king of rasas, the method of piercing has been taught incidentally.
Now, although some have already been stated, I shall explain preparations for rasāyana.

children.text: ādau prātaḥ prātaḥ saindhavayuktaṃ ghṛtaṃ pibettridinam
children.translated_text: First, every morning, one should drink ghee mixed with rock salt for three days;
after that, for three days one should use the decoction called the offspring of ketakī.
The body should be sweated according to rule and made ready with excellent vārtikā;
one should then apply as a purgative the boiled decoction of kaṭurohiṇī.

children.text: tadanu ca śuddhādūrdhvaṃ śleṣmānte recite sakalam
children.translated_text: After that, when purification is complete and all phlegm has been evacuated,
one should use a diet of yāvaka with ghee for three days.

children.text: punarapi ca pānayogaṃ vakṣyāmi ca sakalabhuvanahitakṛtaye
children.translated_text: Again I shall explain a drinking preparation for the benefit of the whole world:
having drunk this powder with hot water in the first watch,
a powder of pathyā, rock salt, dhātrī, pepper, vacā, jaggery, viḍaṅga, and turmeric,
and also of dry ginger and long pepper, should be used for three days.
By this, his body purified, strong, and free from the fault of contact,
having drunk it with milk, he becomes purified by this yāvaka.
If a man applies rasāyana without making the body a prepared field,

children.text: tasya krāmati na rasaḥ sa rasaḥ sarvāṅgadoṣakṛdbhavati ||
children.translated_text: the mercury does not pass through him; that mercury becomes productive of disorders in all the limbs.
Thus, purified, having gained strength, with rice, yāvaka, and the juice called mudga,
having made his own body into a prepared field, he should undertake rasāyana according to rule.
Having churned together cedar oil, ghee, honey, dhātrī juice, and milk,
a man who drinks it becomes one whose bowels are purified, inwardly cleansed.

children.text: māsena kāntimedhe dvābhyāṃ praśamayati doṣanikaraṃ ca
children.translated_text: In one month it brings beauty and intelligence; in two months it also pacifies the mass of doṣas;
and in three months, again, he has taste, a deathless body, and great brilliance.
Cedar oil, ghee, and an equal portion combined with triphalā juice,
when drunk, brings disorders of the eyes to pacification within seven days.

children.text: suratarutailaṃ saghṛtaṃ pītvā śālyodanaṃ ca sakṣīram
children.translated_text: Having drunk cedar oil with ghee, and then rice food with milk,

children.text: jīrṇāhāre bhuktvā harati hi sakuṣṭhān pīnasādīṃśca ||
children.translated_text: eating when the previous food has been digested, it indeed removes skin diseases together with catarrh and the like.
The essence of deathless cedar, accompanied by ghee and joined with oil, destroys diseases arising from vāta and caused by pitta;
when accompanied by jaggery or by honey, it destroys those born of kapha.
One should take rice food with milk, avoiding sour gruel and greens;
the lowest, middle, and highest measures are two, four, and six palas.
After that one should consume <s>sūtaka</s> mercury purified by sublimation, as āroṭa;
there are sweating, stupefaction, raising up, sublimation, blocking, and also the prescribed discipline.
Together with abhraka it is to be sublimed according to rule until it becomes stable;
or else the mercury should be sublimed together with mākṣika according to the procedure.
Thus mercury in the āroṭa state is first employed in making the body a prepared field;

children.text: athavā bhasma ca kṛtvā baddho vā kalkayogena ||
children.translated_text: or else, having made it into ash, or bound by the application of a paste.
With powders of mākṣika, śilājatu, iron, pathyā, akṣa, and viḍaṅga, and with ghee and honey,
one should first employ the combined <s>rasa</s> for making the body a prepared field.
Thus, having eaten mercury made into a paste and combined with ghana, kānta, honey, ghee, and the like,
one reaches immortality; this is the principal preparation of the body as a field.

children.text: atha kṛṣṇaṃ vā pītaṃ vā saṃyojyaṃ ghanaṃ śikhiprabhaṃ bahuśaḥ
children.translated_text: Then black or yellow ghana, shining like fire, should repeatedly be combined;
sprinkled with the milk of a cow and freed from mountain-defect, it is to be used in rasāyana.
Even when pure and without moonlike sheen, it is joined with viḍaṅga, triphalā, ghee, and honey;
eating one pala every day, living on milk, according to rule,
one should eat vyoma together with trikaṭu, viḍaṅga, triphalā, mākṣika, and śilājatu, with milk-rice;
a creature lives for a hundred years.
Such and other preparations, including those joined with sour gruel, have often been taught;
but preparations of leaf-abhraka are to be avoided, for they are without proper rationale.
Those leaf-abhraka preparations that have been prescribed according to rule for the purpose of rasāyana,
by people ignorant of the properties of substances, amount to an instruction in old age and death.
Ghana that has not attained the state fit for the body brings one's digestive fire to pacification;
even without fire, it perishes, overcome by many groups of diseases.

children.text: abhrasya rasāyanināṃ bhakṣyamiha kīrtitaṃ paraṃ satvam
children.translated_text: For those practicing rasāyana, the supreme edible substance of abhraka is here said to be its sattva;

children.text: trividhaṃ gaganamabhakṣyaṃ kācaḥ kiṭṭaṃ ca pattrarajaḥ ||
children.translated_text: three kinds of gagana are inedible: glassy matter, slag, and leaf-dust.
At the beginning, having triturated ghana, iron-dust, and triphalā juice by levigations,
one should make it like collyrium by the rays of the sun, covered with a cloth.
Having thus made it smooth, equal to various powders of kānta iron,

children.text: lohaghanaṃ ca tadevaṃ bhṛṅgeṇa ca sādhayed bahuśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: that iron-ghana should then be processed many times with bhṛṅga.
This nectar, mixed with triphalā, ghee, and honey, kept for a month in grain,
placed inside a casket of steel bowls and worshiped with mantras,

children.text: māsena tu taduddhṛtya jñātvā balaṃ tatprayuñjīta
children.translated_text: should then be taken out after a month; having ascertained its strength, one should use it.

children.text: kāntaṃ vinātha gaganaṃ gaganaṃ vinā tathā ca kāntam ||
children.translated_text: Without kānta there is no gagana, and likewise without gagana there is no kānta.
It destroys obesity, cataract-film, glassy eye disease, darkness of vision, tumors, ringing in the ears, and pains;
it destroys hemorrhoids, fistula, urinary disease, spleen disorders, and also greying of the hair.
While doing this, the wise man should eat chiefly cow's products and buttermilk,
meat of wild animals, mung, ghee, milk, and rice food, while observing celibacy.
One whose ghana-sattva has been digested to a quarter, whose kānta has been digested, and whose sharp metal has been digested equally,
is the supreme prepared field; even āroṭa is again employed.
Ghana-sattva, kānta, and mercury, dead gold, and śatāvarī juice,
licked with ghee and honey for years, destroy death and old age.
Having first made one of these formulas for the purpose of preparing the body as a field,
it should be employed for a year or for half a year for the attainment of the highest good.
With abhraka, sasyaka, mākṣika, rasa, darada, vimala, vajra, and girijatu,
with vaikrānta, kānta, tīkṣṇa iron, gold, silver, and copper,
combined together or separately, with two, three, or four according to availability,
<s>rasendra</s> mercury, digested and killed, is praised by good men for rasāyana.

children.text: viṣanāgavaṅgabaddho bhukto hi rasaḥ karoti kuṣṭhādīn
children.translated_text: Mercury bound with poison, nāga lead, or vaṅga tin, when eaten, produces skin diseases and the like;

children.text: uparasabaddhe tu rase sphuṭanti bhukte tathāṅgāni ||
children.translated_text: but when mercury is bound with secondary minerals and then eaten, the limbs burst apart.
For mercury that has been consumed and digested with ghana-sattva, kānta, kāñcī, bhāskara, and tīkṣṇa iron,
the dose is a guñjā; one māṣaka is the highest dose.
For mercury that pierces a hundredfold the dose is two guñjās; likewise for one that pierces a thousand and one it is one guñjā;

children.text: ardhā ca lakṣavedhinaḥ siddhārthaḥ koṭivedhinaḥ sūtāt ||
children.translated_text: for one that pierces a hundred thousand it is half, and for mercury that pierces ten million it is a siddhārtha seed.
Mercury applied to gold, kānta-stone, and various pills
a man should thus retain while intent on recitation, oblation, and worship of the deity.
Food should consist of preparations made from rice flour, with ghee and soups of mung and meat;

children.text: yavagodhūmānnāni ca gokṣīraṃ mastu ca viśeṣāt ||
children.translated_text: also foods of barley and wheat, cow's milk, and especially buttermilk.

children.text: pāne jalamakṣāraṃ madhurāṇi yāni kāni śastāni
children.translated_text: For drinking, non-alkaline water is recommended, and any sweet things whatever are wholesome.
It should be drunk with the mouth delighted by the fragrance of the four aromatics and camphor.

children.text: madyāranālapānaṃ tailaṃ dadhi vā rase neṣṭam
children.translated_text: Drinking liquor, sour gruel, oil, or curds is not approved in the rasa regimen.
A wise man should not perform an oil massage on the body with pungent oil during rasāyana.

children.text: dagdham apakvam amadhuram uṣṇaṃ kṣīraṃ na naṣṭamāṃsaṃ tu
children.translated_text: Burnt, uncooked, unsweet, hot milk should not be used, nor spoiled meat.
Stale fruits and roots are certainly not prescribed here as food.

children.text: atha laṅghanaṃ na kāryaṃ yāmādho bhojanaṃ naiva
children.translated_text: Now fasting should not be done, and one should not eat after a yāma has passed.
Thus, having set aside what is forbidden, the intelligent man should act with regard to the king of rasas.
Free from worry and anger, he should bathe with pleasant water.
He should not exorcise seizures, fevers, rākṣasas, bhūtas, or mother-goddesses.
Absorbed in the supreme brahman, with tranquil mind, having attained equanimity,
reassuring the three aims of life, having conquered them, he is satisfied with the bliss of rasa.

children.text: yastyaktvā śāstravidhiṃ pravartate svecchayā rase mūḍhaḥ
children.translated_text: The fool who, abandoning the rule of the śāstra, proceeds according to his own desire in rasa,
through his contrary conduct, very serious indigestion arises for him.
When indigestion occurs here, there may be sleepiness, lassitude, fever, darkness, burning,
slight pain in the region below the navel, dullness, loss of appetite, and breaking pain in the limbs.
Having recognized his indigestion in this way, this treatment should be performed to cover it over,
for three days, by a wise man who has set aside the rasāyana.
For three days he should drink a decoction of the root-juice of karkoṭī with salt,
or with sauvarcala salt, or together with cow's urine, in indigestion from rasa.

children.text: piṣṭvātha mātuluṅgīṃ pibati rasaṃ śuṇṭhisaindhavaṃ prātaḥ
children.translated_text: Or, having ground mātuluṅgī, he drinks its juice in the morning with dry ginger and rock salt;

children.text: kvathitaṃ gosalilena tu rakṣati samyak rasājīrṇam ||
children.translated_text: boiled with cow's urine, it properly guards against rasa-induced indigestion.
If in some way, through ignorance, rasa contaminated with nāga and the like has been eaten,
then, to drive it out, he should drink cow's urine with the roots of bitter kāravallī.
Śarapuṅkhā, suradālī, paṭola, bimbī, and kākamācī,
if any one of these is mentioned, he should take it when boiled in indigestion.
With excessively sour, salty, and pungent things, a flowing away of rasa and wasting occur;
and with excessively sweet things, and with constant eating, the digestive fire is destroyed.

children.text: yaḥ punarevaṃ satataṃ karoti mūḍhaḥ samāhāram
children.translated_text: But the fool who constantly makes such a full meal,

children.text: tasya vinaśyatyagnirna khalu krāmati raso bhaved vyādhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: his fire is destroyed; the rasa certainly does not pass through, and disease arises.
But he who, because he can bear a great digestive fire, is lord of rasa that pierces hundreds, thousands, and lakhs,
succeeds by this procedure, through effort and through the discipline of rasa practice.
Rasa piercing hundreds, thousands, lakhs, crores, arbudas, or even nirbudas,

children.text: piṣṭaṃ bhuñjīta rasaṃ balisahitaṃ siddhido bhavati ||
children.translated_text: when ground and eaten together with an offering, becomes a giver of siddhi.

children.text: krāmati tato hi sūto janayati putrāṃśca devagarbhābhān
children.translated_text: Then indeed the mercury passes through and generates sons like embryos of gods;
and among women he becomes of steady desire, freed from wrinkles and gray hair.

children.text: buddhirbalaṃ prabhāvaḥ saha cāyuṣā vardhate rasāyaninaḥ
children.translated_text: Intellect, strength, and power, together with lifespan, increase for the rasāyana practitioner.
When he has attained divine intelligence, divine qualities also increase.
Thus perfected by rasa, virtuous and free from pain, old age, and death,
by sky-going he constantly travels through all the worlds.
He is a giver in the three worlds, and here he is a creator like the lotus-born one.
He may be a sustainer like <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and he becomes a destroyer like <s>Rudra</s>.
Lodestone, mica-essence, gold, silver, and copper are to be reckoned in equal parts;

children.text: baddhaṃ sūtasamāṃśaṃ dhmātaṃ golaṃ kṛtaṃ khoṭam ||
children.translated_text: bound with an equal part of mercury, blown, and made into a sphere and then a khoṭa.

children.text: bāhye rasena liptaṃ vadanagataṃ śastravārakaṃ rogān
children.translated_text: Smeared externally with mercury and placed in the mouth, it wards off weapons and diseases,
and indeed destroys those situated in the body; it is the pill named Amṛtasundarī.

children.text: yaḥ pūrvoktaḥ sūto lakṣādūrdhvaṃ ca vedhate lohān
children.translated_text: The mercury previously described, which pierces metals beyond a lakh,
when bound by sāraṇa procedures and placed in the mouth, can digest a jewel.
Combined with equal parts of lead, divine iron, lodestone, and pyrite-essences,
together with mica-essence, the pill is named Mṛtasaṃjīvanī.

children.text: hemayutā gulucchake mukuṭe vā kaṇṭhasūtrakarṇe vā
children.translated_text: Joined with gold, whether in a bracelet, crown, necklace, or earring,
it averts the mass of fear of death, grief, disease, poison, weapons, old age, and continual suffering.
On whose body this pill named Mṛtasaṃjīvanī is placed,
he becomes most worthy of worship by asuras, yakṣas, kinnaras, and foremost siddha-yogins.

children.text: prakṣālya toyamadhye guṭikā ghaṭikādvayaṃ tataḥ kṣiptvā
children.translated_text: Having washed it in water, and then having placed the pill there for two ghaṭikās,
this same pill, placed in the mouth, causes a dead man to rise.

children.text: toyaṃ tadeva pibati svasthaṃ pathyānvitastataḥ puruṣaḥ
children.translated_text: Then the man, healthy and following the proper regimen, drinks that very water;
he obtains a divine body, firm, free from death and old age.

children.text: kāntaghanasattvakamalaṃ hema ca tāraṃ yathā kṛtadvandvam
children.translated_text: Lodestone, dense essence, lotus, gold, and silver, paired as prescribed,
equally digested, with the best seed and joined with diamond, is the Vajriṇī pill.
When this is placed in the cavity of the mouth, it produces strength equal to a young elephant.
That body too becomes hard to pierce, free from death, old age, and disease.
When the rasa has been treated by smoke, digested with the five great jewels, and made sārita,
with seed, in mica-essence, applied with pyrites and lodestone,
the pill called Khecarī flies when merely placed in the mouth.
He becomes most worthy of worship by hosts of gods, asuras, and siddhas, and by <s>Indra</s> and the others.
Rasavāda, possessing endless qualities, is divided according to liquid, sphere, and paste.
Those men by whom it has been understood, taught by the foremost siddhas, are victorious.
Born in the lunar dynasty, born in the <s>Haihaya</s> family, with glory produced by his qualities,
glorious <s>Madana</s>, lord of the Kirātas and teacher of rasa, is victorious.
In him rasa-knowledge, the support of all auspiciousness, has itself descended.
The cause of the highest good is the highest good of the supreme lord, as stated before.
Therefore, having received great honor from the <s>Kirāta</s> king, and being devoted to the work of rasa,
the monk <s>Govinda</s> composed the tantra called <s>Rasahṛdaya</s>.
